concepts.rationale: The two original recipes directly support sweet and savory baked pasta bound with eggs and dairy. PRO TV explicitly names its savory preparation budinca de paste. This makes the descriptive label accurate without implying all pasta with cheese is already pudding.

The original Bucate Aromate recipe mixes eggs with milk, pours the mixture into caramel, bakes in a water bath, then cools and inverts it. Gina Bradea independently documents the same familiar dessert. The definition describes custard, not pastry cream.

The separately identified cocoa and chocolate cake bases in the two original recipes support tray baking and the ordinary Romanian cake label. Robert Eisler independently identifies the cake and square portions. No ethnic or origin claim is present.

The original recipe bakes and cools the meringue base before whipped cream and fruit assembly. A Romanian publication from 2009 and PRO TV broadcast from September 2022 support established local exposure. The proposal makes no disputed country-of-origin claim.

Gina Bradea directly describes small baked choux shells, filling after cooling and chocolate sauce, with ice cream in the served version. A 2025 Pizza Hut Romania menu independently documents commercial use of the name. The definition remains distinct from an elongated eclair.

items.rationale: The televised original preparation combines boiled pasta with cheese, egg and sour cream and bakes until set. Reusing cooked pasta with cheese then adding egg binding is consistent with the existing concept and the named pudding.

Laura Laurentiu supports boiled pasta, sweet cheese, egg, sugar, raisins and baking. AVE Romania page 64 independently specifies water-soaked raisins in a baked pasta pudding. Water hydration is an explicitly supported alcohol-free variation, not a claim that the first source used water.

Milk and caramel form a factual alternate cue for the same custard. The explanation still explicitly supplies eggs, baking in a water bath, cooling and inversion; it never suggests milk alone sets the custard.
The source uses an uncooked egg-and-milk mixture over caramel in a vessel placed in water, followed by baking and cooling. Both chosen concepts and the disclosed milk match this process.

The source separately labels its chocolate-and-butter negresa base, with eggs, sugar and flour. The proposal represents that baked base; it does not claim the later cheesecake or raspberry additions are required.

The original cocoa cake recipe mixes flour and cocoa with sugar, water, oil and leavening before tray baking. The explanation accurately discloses the additional ingredients and cooking transformation.
The source finishes a baked, fully cooled meringue base with whipped cream and fruit. The explanation preserves the existing cooked meringue state and supplies the omitted fruit.
Fresh fruit over whipped cream on cooled baked meringue is the source assembly. The second pair selects another defining component without converting finished meringue back into raw foam.

The original chocolate sauce combines chocolate and whipping cream with butter, matching a fluid ganache. Baked and cooled filled shells are explicitly prepared before sauce is added; this is a supported serving variation.

The original recipe bakes small choux mounds, cools and fills the shells, and serves them with ice cream and chocolate sauce. The explanation retains this order rather than filling raw dough or reshaping an eclair.

world_rationale: All five definitions and ten recipe ideas have independently checked source support. Prepared ingredient states and cooking/assembly stages are preserved. Additional water-hydration evidence supports the explicitly alcohol-free raisin wording.
